pr_title: Identify F# single case discriminated unions as SumType
pr_body:
Unlike discriminated unions with more than two cases, single case discriminated unions do not inherit from an abstract base class, thus, for single case discriminated unions we need to look for the CompilationMappingAttribute on the type itself.

Single case discriminated unions do have a declared instance member named "Item", so the `FSharpUnionCaseTypeDescription` [correctly identifies this](https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/blob/main/src/Orleans.CodeGenerator/SyntaxGeneration/FSharpUtils.cs#L110).

Fixes #8715

issue_context.title: F# single case discriminated unions not serialized correctly
issue_context.body:
We are upgrading to Orleans 7 in a project using F#. When using single case discriminated unions as arguments to a grain interface, the serializer fails to serialize the argument correctly.

The [attached solution](https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/files/13317800/FSharpHelloWorld.zip), based on the [F#-sample](https://github.com/dotnet/samples/tree/main/orleans/FSharpHelloWorld), reproduces the issue. When running the solution, the value of `SingleCaseDiscriminatedUnion.Case` is `null` when received in `HelloGrain`.

_This is the single case discriminated union we're trying to serialize._
```fsharp
[<GenerateSerializer>]
type SingleCaseDiscriminatedUnion =
    | Case of string // the string is null when received in the grain
``` 

_This is the grain where we're using the single case discriminated union._
```fsharp
type HelloGrain() = 
    inherit Orleans.Grain()
    interface IHelloGrain with
        override this.SayHello(message) =
            let greeting = SingleCaseDiscriminatedUnion.value message // greeting is now null
            ValueTask.FromResult greeting
```

Including a second case in the discriminated union makes the test work.

Related issue #8255
comments: I have attempted a fix for this issue in pull request #8739

review_comments: Do we ever need to worry about deeper inheritance chains than this?
Not that I know of. There is however an issue with DUs of 4 cases or more, but not due to inheritance. I will open separate issue for that.
